items.title: Stanford AI API Gateway
items.text:
Stanford users with an eligible AI API Gateway key can choose Stanford AI API Gateway on a workstation, in a container, on Terra or on Carina.

  1. Run heartwood, or open browser settings where the browser interface is available.
  2. Choose Stanford AI API Gateway.
  3. Enter the gateway key at the hidden prompt.
  4. Choose a model the gateway returns for that key.
  5. Review the route and the action-review setting.

Heartwood uses OpenHands' model-capability registry to select the gateway's Chat Completions or Responses route. The gateway is an institution-managed service, but using it does not authorize a dataset or workflow; Stanford's eligibility, data classification, Data Risk Assessment and project approval requirements apply. See the Stanford AI API Gateway service page, and run a synthetic tool task before using a newly enabled model with research data.

items.title: OpenAI API or Anthropic API
items.text:
1. Run heartwood, or open browser settings.
  2. Choose OpenAI API or Anthropic.
  3. Enter the provider API key when prompted.
  4. Choose a model the provider API returns.
  5. Review the route and the action-review setting.

Heartwood checks that the credential binding, route, model profile and platform policy agree before enabling requests. For OpenAI models that support the Responses API, Heartwood follows OpenHands' registry and authorizes /v1/responses; other models use Chat Completions. The request path is chosen automatically and shared by every interface. Anthropic uses an API key because OpenHands provides no supported Claude subscription sign-in.

items.title: Other Compatible Services
items.text: Choose Other compatible service for an authorized endpoint that implements the OpenAI-compatible requests the selected model needs. Enter the base URL, select or enter a model, and provide an API key only if the service requires one. The route is available on workstations, in containers and on Terra when the active policy permits user-defined routes; Carina does not offer it. Heartwood records the selected catalog and completion endpoints in the project policy before making requests, and a model that OpenHands identifies as Responses-capable needs /responses on the service as well.

items.title: Connect to an Existing Model Server
items.text:
A model server you started yourself is an Other compatible service, even on the same machine. Enter its /v1 base URL and the model identifier it serves.

From a native installation, a loopback server is usually http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1, with no key unless the server requires one. Inside a Heartwood container, 127.0.0.1 is the container itself. Docker Desktop provides http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1; on Linux Docker Engine, add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway to docker run first.

Run with Heartwood is different: Heartwood downloads or imports the model files and supervises its own runtime over a private socket, as described in Run a Model With Heartwood.

items.title: Credentials
items.text:
Heartwood does not accept provider API keys as command-line arguments and never writes API keys or subscription tokens to project configuration, session events, logs, browser storage or audit exports. In a local launch, the model client and the agent's tools share the Heartwood process identity, so the credential is application-scrubbed rather than process-isolated. With such a credential, every action set waits for you; Review Changes requires a credential-free or platform-isolated route, as described in Review Modes.

Heartwood resolves an API key in this order:

  1. a value entered for the running process;
  2. an operator-provided environment or mounted-file binding;
  3. a key saved in the operating-system credential store on a workstation; or
  4. a platform identity or secret mechanism supplied by the deployment.

Where a system credential store is available, the browser offers Remember securely for this project and heartwood setup accepts --remember-credential. The saved entry is scoped to the project and provider; the project configuration keeps only non-secret model settings. Keys for Other compatible service stay process-only, because changing the service URL changes the trust boundary. ChatGPT sign-in credentials stay in OpenHands' user-level store so that the account can be refreshed and reused across projects.

Forget a saved credential from the browser or terminal:

heartwood models forget openai
heartwood models forget anthropic
heartwood models forget stanford-ai-api-gateway
heartwood models forget openai-subscription

An isolated worker never receives the provider credential: it gets an OpenShell placeholder, which the provider attachment outside the worker resolves.

items.title: Command-Line Catalog Operations
items.text:
heartwood models refresh openai-subscription
heartwood models refresh openai
heartwood models connect openai MODEL_ID
heartwood models validate

These commands serve diagnostics and automation. Guided setup remains the normal path because it collects credentials without exposing them in shell history and explains unavailable choices.

items.title: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment
items.text:
Heartwood can package the model selected in a connected project as a bundle and verify it into a project without network access. The bundle holds the immutable model source, license record, runtime settings, selected files and a SHA-256 digest for every file. It imports into a local launch's .heartwood/models/.

The bundle does not authorize the transfer or approve the model for a dataset. Use an institution-approved transfer channel and review the displayed license and warnings before import.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
You need:

  • the same Heartwood release in the connected and offline environments;
  • connected storage for the selected model plus one uncompressed bundle;
  • destination storage for the bundle, the imported model and a 512 MiB import reserve;
  • a model runtime that matches the destination compute; and
  • an approved way to move the bundle between environments.

Keep the bundle out of source control and container images.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: 1. Prepare the Model While Connected
items.text:
Enter the project that already uses the model, or create a staging project and download one:

mkdir heartwood-model-staging
cd heartwood-model-staging
heartwood models download qwen25-7b-instruct-q4_k_m
heartwood doctor

heartwood models managed lists the catalog for the detected environment. For another Hugging Face model, follow Other Hugging Face Models first.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: 2. Create the Bundle
items.text:
Create the destination directory, then export the model selected in the current project:

mkdir -p /approved-transfer
heartwood models export /approved-transfer/heartwood-model.heartwood-model.zip

Heartwood verifies the source model, hashes the bytes again while writing, and never replaces an existing file. Exporting unchanged model files and metadata again produces the same bundle bytes. The terminal and browser report byte progress and can cancel an export without publishing a partial bundle.

Move the completed .heartwood-model.zip file through the approved transfer process, without provider credentials or other .heartwood/ content.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: 3. Inspect the Bundle in the Destination
items.text:
Enter an empty destination project and inspect the bundle before changing anything:

mkdir offline-analysis
cd offline-analysis
heartwood models inspect-bundle /approved-transfer/heartwood-model.heartwood-model.zip

Review the model, immutable revision, license, runtime, file count, size and platform warnings. Checksums establish that imported files match the bundle, not who supplied it. Heartwood therefore ignores any qualification a bundle claims: a model that exactly matches the installed catalog uses the catalog's qualification, and every other imported model is Not tested. For a vLLM directory the catalog pins the upstream revision but not the file contents, so import vLLM bundles only from a transfer path you control.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: 4. Approve and Import
items.text:
heartwood models import /approved-transfer/heartwood-model.heartwood-model.zip

Heartwood shows the review again and asks for explicit license approval; --approve-license gives that decision for reviewed automation. The import is bound to the manifest you reviewed and stops if the bundle changes before copying begins. It streams each file into private staging, checks its size and digest, verifies the runtime-specific model structure, publishes the model atomically under .heartwood/models/, and selects it in the project configuration. If it is cancelled or selection fails, fully verified files stay in the model cache and are verified again on retry; incomplete staging is removed.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: 5. Verify and Start
items.text:
heartwood doctor
heartwood runtime start --dry-run
heartwood

The runtime planner uses the transferred files and settings exactly as for a connected download and never fetches them from Hugging Face after a restart.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Use the Browser or Notebook
items.text:
Where the browser interface is available, open Settings → Models → Move a model between environments. Export and import use paths visible to the server rather than uploading files through the page, and show the same plan, warnings, progress, cancellation and final selection as the terminal.

The notebook bridge calls the same gateway operations:

from pathlib import Path

from heartwood.notebook import NotebookSession

with NotebookSession() as session:
    plan = session.inspect_model_bundle(
        Path("/approved-transfer/heartwood-model.heartwood-model.zip")
    )
    transfer = session.import_model_bundle(
        Path(plan["bundle_path"]),
        approved=True,
        manifest_sha256=plan["manifest_sha256"],
    )

Use the terminal or browser for the license review unless the notebook workflow has an equivalent human approval step.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Run a Container Without Networking
items.text:
After the bundle is imported into the mounted project, a terminal-only container can run without a network namespace:

docker run --rm -it \
  --network none \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --env HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
  ghcr.io/schmiedmayerlab/heartwood:0.5.0 \
  heartwood

Docker's none network removes external interfaces and keeps container-local loopback. The bind mount still exposes the current host directory, so this is a network boundary, not host isolation, and there is no browser route.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Recover From an Interrupted Transfer
items.text:
• If an export stopped, confirm that the output path holds no completed bundle and export again.
  • If an import stopped, rerun the same import; private incomplete staging is removed first.
  • If the bundle changed after review, inspect it again and investigate the transfer channel rather than bypassing the error.
  • If checksums or the file list do not match, obtain a new bundle from the connected project.
  • If the destination already holds different files, use a clean project, or remove the model only after confirming that no project needs it.
  • If the runtime is unavailable or incompatible, install the matching Heartwood runtime or choose a model the destination supports; importing weights installs no drivers or inference software.

Importing the same unchanged bundle again verifies the existing copy and returns it without duplicating storage.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Verify the Offline Boundary
items.text:
Before using project data, confirm that:

  • the active model is Heartwood-managed and no hosted model credential is configured;
  • the platform independently denies outbound network traffic;
  • project and model storage meet the environment's handling requirements; and
  • audit exports stay in approved storage.

CI runs the connected export, a no-network import into a read-only container, the runtime plan, real model inference, an OpenHands tool proposal, approval and rejection, file checks, replay and audit export as one acceptance path on Linux AMD64. Transfer authorization and the environment's network isolation remain infrastructure responsibilities.
path: Move a Model Into an Offline Environment

items.title: Run a Model With Heartwood
items.text: Heartwood images and the native packages include inference software but no model weights. Once a supported model is downloaded or imported, heartwood verifies its files, plans the context against available memory, starts the runtime, waits until it is ready, and opens the requested interface. A cached model avoids the download, but Heartwood still verifies its source revision and file hashes before every start. Heartwood-managed models run for local launches; an isolated worker uses the HTTPS model endpoint set in its deployment manifest.

items.title: Download and Start
items.text:
heartwood

Choose Run with Heartwood, inspect the plan, and confirm the download. The terminal shows transferred bytes and status; the browser shows a progress bar from the same gateway download state.

In the terminal, Heartwood continues automatically after the verified download and starts the runtime. In the browser setup flow, stop the process and run heartwood --interface web again when the page reports that the model is ready; the new process verifies the model, starts the runtime and supervises it for the session.

Stopping the gateway cancels unfinished downloads and waits for their workers. A shutdown timeout means work is still running; wait for it and retry the shutdown before moving project state. Verified model files remain available for the next launch.

items.title: Runtime Connection and Lifetime
items.text: The launcher gives llama.cpp or vLLM a private Unix socket in an owner-only temporary directory outside the project. Readiness checks, model discovery and inference use that socket, and no managed TCP listener is opened; the http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1 address in model settings is a logical route for the SDK's private transport, not a port to connect to. A missing socket or altered route stops inference instead of falling back to another listener. If the runtime exits, the launcher stops the interaction, and it removes the socket directory on shutdown; a new runtime needs a new Heartwood process. Other processes running as the same user keep that user's access; the isolated worker deployment is the boundary that separates agent code from the runtime.

items.title: Hardware
items.text:
Runtime Model Shape Typical Environment llama.cpp One GGUF file CPU workstation, standard container or native Linux vLLM Standard safetensors snapshot NVIDIA GPU container, Terra GPU image or a Carina Slurm GPU allocation

Heartwood reports model-specific minimum and recommended resources before download. For GPU configurations it also checks the catalog GPU count, per-device memory, driver, precision, tool parser, tensor-parallel layout and qualification status against the GPU compatibility matrix. No static estimate covers every architecture, driver, concurrent workload or platform limit.

items.title: Context Window
items.text:
Heartwood records the model's declared limit and chooses a conservative operating tier that fits the available memory.

Tier OpenHands Input Reserved for the Response 18,432 16,384 2,048 32,768 28,672 4,096

18,432 tokens is the smallest agent-capable tier, and Heartwood uses it whenever model-size or memory information is unavailable. Larger tiers range from 65,536 up to the model limit and Heartwood's maximum of 1,048,576 tokens. Before history exceeds the input budget, OpenHands condenses it, keeping recent events and a summary. A larger window helps with broad repositories and long analyses but increases key/value-cache memory and latency, so prefer the largest window that fits with headroom over the value on a model card.

items.title: Advanced Runtime Control
items.text:
Start with heartwood. Operators can inspect or control runtime allocation separately:

heartwood runtime start --dry-run
heartwood runtime start --task-profile powerful --partition dev --time 01:00:00

On Carina, Heartwood prints the complete Slurm request and asks before allocating GPUs; on Terra it uses the attached resources without a scheduler request. Download and allocation are confirmed separately. --dry-run can show a recommendation when no model is selected, but never saves it; complete setup before starting or allocating the runtime.

items.title: Stop the Runtime
items.text: Exit Heartwood to stop the supervised runtime. Downloaded model files remain in .heartwood/models/ and are verified again on the next start.

items.title: Deploy Heartwood
items.text: A Heartwood deployment combines a pinned release artifact with the platform's storage, identity, network, secret, compute, model-route, logging and data-governance controls. Read Support and Compatibility before selecting a release, and Security and Controlled Data before choosing an execution shape.

items.title: Deployment Responsibilities
items.text:
Layer Heartwood provides Platform or institution provides Application Gateway, terminal, browser and notebook interfaces, OpenHands adapter, Skills, policy, action review, audit Artifact approval and release selection Project Research-file boundary; local .heartwood/ state, or protected state bound by the deployment manifest Durable storage, permissions, backup, retention and deletion Execution Local execution, or an isolated OpenShell worker with gateway-side admission, fencing and revocation Docker engine, sandbox gateway, mandatory filesystem and network enforcement Identity Launch capability on every gateway request, credential bindings, credential-boundary checks User authentication and authorization, capability delivery, secret delivery, managed identities Models Provider catalogs, route-policy evaluation, Heartwood-managed inference planning Approved endpoints, agreements, accounts, quotas and data eligibility Network Deny-by-default model-route policy and declared ingress validation Enforced egress, authenticated ingress, proxy header sanitation, TLS and segmentation Evidence Session events, hash-chained audit, scrubbed export, signed checkpoints, deployment-bound evidence gates Signer authorization and key custody, records storage and retention, monitoring, incident response

The Platform Contract defines this boundary for platform partners, and Platform API and Access Requirements lists what to request from a platform operator.

items.title: Select an Artifact
items.text:
• The standard image (ghcr.io/schmiedmayerlab/heartwood) is published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
  • The NVIDIA image (-gpu-nvidia tags) is linux/amd64 only; match its configuration against the GPU compatibility matrix.
  • The Terra images (-terra and -terra-gpu-nvidia tags) are single-platform linux/amd64 images for Terra Leonardo.
  • The native installer and archive are for platforms where containers are not the normal execution mechanism.

Pin a release tag or digest; do not deploy the moving edge tags. Releases do not publish a worker image or a sandbox gateway. For an isolated worker, build the worker target of docker-bake.hcl from the release commit, record its image identifier, and qualify it with the sandbox gateway you deploy.

items.title: Deployment Manifest
items.text:
The deployment manifest is an operator-owned TOML file that binds one research directory to protected state, a policy ceiling and, optionally, an isolated worker and managed evidence. Configuration and State specifies every key, with a complete example. It is read only by heartwood gateway serve --deployment PATH, heartwood project migrate --deployment PATH --backup PATH and heartwood project recover-migration --deployment PATH:

heartwood gateway serve --deployment /etc/heartwood/projects/research.toml

Start the command from the exact research directory the manifest names. The standalone terminal, NotebookSession() and heartwood audit commands never read a manifest, so researchers reach a bound project through the gateway's browser interface or a client of its API. Keep the manifest and every file it names outside the research directory and the state directory, owned by root or the gateway user and not writable by group or others; any violation, unknown key or invalid value stops startup before a store is opened. Existing local .heartwood/ state is never adopted silently; move it with heartwood project migrate, as described in Operator-Bound External State.

items.title: Policy Ceiling
items.text: The [policy] table replaces the platform adapter's built-in policy as the ceiling for the project, and project settings can only narrow it. platform_id must equal the detected platform adapter, and deny_egress_by_default must stay true. When allowed_action_review_modes is omitted, all three modes are permitted, and a session in an isolated worker with no researcher selection uses review-outside-effects. Set the list explicitly; Action Review describes each mode and the evidence required before listing it.

items.title: Isolated Worker
items.text:
A [worker] table runs each session's agent in an OpenShell sandbox on a local Docker engine. Without it, the agent runs in the gateway process even though state is protected. Take sandbox_policy_sha256 and image_digest from qualification, not from the worker whose admission they decide. Membership in the Docker socket's group grants control-plane authority; never add a worker identity to it.

gateway_versions lists every version string the registered sandbox gateway may report and that your qualification evidence covers. Before serving, and before each worker launch or reconciliation, Heartwood reads the gateway's version through its Health API and stops with HW-WORKER-001 when it is missing or not listed. The qualification build reports 0.1.8+heartwood.2. The check compares your declaration with the gateway's own report; it does not establish that the gateway has the behavior native qualification depends on.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: An [evidence] table binds automatic signed checkpoints to an independently authorized signer and records service. It requires a [worker] table; see Configure Managed Evidence for its keys.

items.title: Persist the Right Data
items.text:
Assign one dedicated project directory as the process current directory. Persist research files and canonical state separately from installation files, temporary runtime files and job scratch. Local launches use .heartwood/ in the project; manifest launches use state_root. Back up the research files and their matching state together, and preserve the project identity on restore. Never mount the state directory or the manifest into a worker.

Do not pre-create .heartwood/ with another layout. Opening the browser and running heartwood doctor are read-only; project confirmation or the first mutating operation initializes state.

items.title: Provide Model Connections
items.text: Built-in connections and operator-configured compatible routes are checked against the active policy's endpoints, credential references and capability tiers. The model-connection manifest schema exists, but startup does not load it. Never place raw tokens in container layers, image labels, project configuration, command arguments, examples or CI logs. An isolated worker uses only the [worker] model route, and its real credential stays in the OpenShell provider.

items.title: Validate the Deployment
items.text:
Before real data, use a synthetic project to verify:

  1. the artifact digest and the GET /project/capabilities response;
  2. project persistence across process or compute restart;
  3. model discovery and a real agent response with a structured tool proposal;
  4. grouped approve and reject behavior, and that only the intended review modes are offered;
  5. for an isolated worker, outside denial of protected state, control-plane access and unapproved egress, and revocation before writer release;
  6. terminal, browser and notebook parity where advertised;
  7. replay and scrubbed audit export with no secret values in configuration, events, logs or exports;
  8. ingress host, origin, forwarding, prefix and source rejection;
  9. the reported model-credential boundary;
  10. enforced network behavior, including a no-network Heartwood-managed inference test when offline operation is claimed; and
  11. signed checkpoint creation, external retention, independent verification and synthetic restore.

Concurrent advisory reviews require their own evidence; see Qualify Parallel Reviews. Keep validation records with the deployment's operating documentation and never include protected data in a fixture or transcript.

items.title: Record a Standard Environment
items.text:
When several researchers share one setup, keep one record of it outside every research project and verify each researcher's environment against it before project data is added.

Record Source Release tag and verified digest Select an Artifact Deployment manifest and its digest Deployment Manifest Platform image, compute shape and storage The platform guide, such as Terra Approved model routes Choose a Model Route Permitted review modes Action Review Signer profile and checkpoint retention Audit Checkpoints and Retention Analysis dependency lock Verify an Existing Analysis Owner and next update review Support and Compatibility

items.title: Run a Pilot Evaluation
items.text:
A pilot shows whether a small group can install, use and trust one standard environment before a wider rollout. Use synthetic or approved non-sensitive data, keep the release pinned, and name a support contact.

  1. Agree on exit criteria before the first participant starts.
  2. Onboard each participant until they have made one action decision.
  3. Have every participant run the three research workflows in order on the same synthetic inputs.
  4. Collect the evidence below, then list the changes a wider rollout or a second platform requires.
Question Evidence Could participants start? Installation success and time to the first action decision Did the workflows complete and reproduce? heartwood experiments list --json and the verification report Is the record intact? heartwood audit verify What did support require? Requests and time to resolution Would participants use it? Structured feedback

Collect counts and outcomes, not prompts, project files or session history. Report the results as live synthetic validation of that environment; see Testing and Evidence.

items.title: Audit Checkpoints and Retention
items.text:
Every session keeps a content-minimized, hash-chained audit record. A signed checkpoint authenticates one export of it, with a signed deployment and retention statement, for storage outside the agent-writable project. Its authority comes from independently trusted keys, signer authorization and the records system's own controls.

There are two ways to create checkpoints:

  • the explicit heartwood audit checkpoint command, which uses local project state and does not read the deployment manifest; and
  • deployment-bound managed evidence, selected by the manifest's [evidence] table, which checkpoints automatically and gates dispatch.

Checkpoint creation is not a gateway HTTP route.

items.title: Choose the Right Artifact
items.text:
Artifact Use Storage Session replay Inspect private conversation and action history Session state in the project's state directory Scrubbed audit export Review or transfer content-minimized operational events A reviewed temporary destination Signed audit checkpoint Preserve an authenticated export with deployment and retention metadata Deployment-controlled records storage outside the project

A checkpoint directory contains audit.jsonl and checkpoint.json, and optionally experiments.jsonl. Its signature covers the canonical audit digest, event count, terminal chain hash, session, deployment identifier, creation time, retention declaration, signer identity, key identifier, key version, algorithm and public-key fingerprint.

items.title: Evidence Boundaries
items.text: Verifying one checkpoint establishes its integrity and authenticity against the selected key. It does not establish continuity between checkpoints, detect an omitted later checkpoint, or prove that the signer observed the recorded actions. A valid hash chain alone cannot rule out a history rewritten and rehashed before signing, and worker-reported results remain claims unless the destination or the outside control plane verifies them. Signed retention dates do not prove that the records system enforced immutability, availability or deletion.

items.title: Automatic Evidence Boundaries
items.text:
Managed evidence checkpoints every approval and rejection decision and the closure of a session owner. Closing an owner releases its writer lease; it does not delete the session. Each checkpoint binds the previous checkpoint's digest and extends its exact audit prefix, and the signer validates project, session, deployment, retention policy and complete retained history before publishing it. The records adapter uses conditional writes, version-aware reads and COMPLIANCE retention observations, and rejects hidden versions, delete markers, missing ordinals and changed retained bytes.

In required mode, a decision stays pending until its checkpoint has been read back and verified from retained storage. The evidence policy is retained with the decision, so removing the [evidence] table or switching to buffered cannot downgrade a pending decision. In buffered mode, ordinary work continues during a records or signing outage with a visible evidence gap. Approved outside operations and outside-result releases require retained evidence in both modes; a signature without observed retention never satisfies that gate.

An outside approval is recorded as authorized, checkpointed, then marked submitting before the native call. It is submitted only by an exact retry of its own approval command, after current input, policy, expiry, destination and worker checks; reads and reconciliation never submit it. Once submission may have occurred, Heartwood observes the native operation instead of repeating it.

Managed evidence does not checkpoint every model request, prove a worker's claims, or qualify the signing service or storage. AnchoredCheckpointSigner in heartwood.audit composes the signer and records interfaces for an independent signing authority, but it is a library, not a deployed service: the operator supplies authenticated hosting, caller-to-scope authorization, key custody and storage policy.

items.title: Configure Managed Evidence
items.text:
Add an [evidence] table to the deployment manifest. It requires a [worker] table and protected project identity, and Heartwood never reads records credentials, endpoints or signer selections from project content.

[evidence]
mode = "required"
deployment_id = "research-production"
endpoint = "https://records.example.org"
region = "us-east-1"
bucket = "research-audit-records"
prefix = "heartwood/project-a"
signer_registry = "/etc/heartwood/checkpoint-signers.toml"
signer_profile = "research-records"
previous_signer_profiles = []
credential_process = "/usr/local/libexec/heartwood-records-credentials"

[evidence.retention]
policy_id = "research-records-retention"
retain_until = "2033-12-31"
Key Meaning mode required or buffered deployment_id, region Identifiers of letters, digits, _, . and - endpoint HTTPS service origin with no credentials, path, query or fragment bucket Existing S3 bucket name prefix Slash-separated prefix of letters, digits, _ and - retention policy_id and retain_until as YYYY-MM-DD; an expired date prevents startup signer_registry, signer_profile Registry path and a production-mode profile in it previous_signer_profiles Unique profile names accepted only to verify retained history after key rotation credential_process Executable returning version-1 credential-process JSON credentials_file, credentials_profile Owner-only AWS shared-credentials file and the profile in it ca_bundle Optional operator-controlled CA file for the records service

Select exactly one credential source: credential_process, or credentials_file with credentials_profile. All paths are absolute and must be operator-owned, write-protected and outside research files and state. The credential process runs without arguments from its own directory, with a fifteen-second deadline and a 64 KiB output limit, and its error output is not shown; include Expiration for temporary credentials. See the SDK credential-process contract. A shared credentials file is read once per gateway lifetime, so use the credential process when credentials must refresh during a session. Ambient proxy, profile, endpoint, certificate, environment and metadata credentials are never used as fallbacks, and no credential reaches the worker.

Restart the gateway after changing the signer profile, token or trust set, and confirm continuity before resuming work. Do not edit a retained scope's retention declaration; exact scope validation rejects that change.

items.title: Records Permissions and Retention
items.text:
Use an existing versioned bucket with Object Lock and an independently administered retention policy; Heartwood neither creates the bucket nor grants storage privileges. Each session has a deterministic namespace under prefix, with candidates, experiments and checkpoints children.

Principal Read access Write access Gateway Version listing, exact object versions and retention metadata within its scope Conditional candidate and experiment creation with the declared retention Signing authority Authorized candidates and complete retained checkpoint history with retention metadata Conditional checkpoint creation with the declared retention Worker None None

On Amazon S3, the adapter uses s3:ListBucketVersions, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectRetention, plus s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectRetention on each principal's writable prefixes. Scope list permissions with prefix conditions and object permissions with exact resource patterns; encryption may need separately scoped key permissions. See S3 operation permissions and Object Lock visibility. Neither identity needs bucket administration, object deletion, governance bypass, ACL changes or access to another prefix. Enforce If-None-Match writes in the bucket policy as well, because versioning and retention alone do not prevent a new version from hiding an older one. See S3 conditional-write enforcement. Qualify equivalent behavior for any other S3-compatible store.

A working manifest does not prove that the signer authorizes requests, that the storage identities are restricted, or that the institution approves the deployment. Verify authorized and denied operations, key rotation, interrupted publication, retention, backup and restore, and network boundaries with synthetic records before admitting sensitive data.

items.title: Infrastructure Telemetry
items.text:
OpenShell can export its native OCSF events through OTLP to an authenticated collector. Configure the sandbox gateway's openshell.gateway.otlp.ocsf section with enabled, the collector endpoint, and operator-controlled ca_file, cert_file and key_file paths, and require a collector that validates client certificates. Correlate openshell.gateway.name and openshell.sandbox.id with the worker attempt, and keep native event identifiers for deduplication.

Delivery is best effort and can repeat records. An openshell.ocsf.gap event reports dropped records through openshell.ocsf.gap.dropped and openshell.ocsf.gap.since_unix_ms, but its absence does not prove complete collection. Heartwood does not gate dispatch on collector health; stopping work when observation is unavailable needs outside enforcement. Infrastructure events do not replace the canonical decision record. See Infrastructure Telemetry qualification.

items.title: Understand Configuration Ownership
items.text:
Scope Default location Contents Project config.toml in the state directory An approved signer profile name only Managed deployment /etc/heartwood/checkpoint-signers.toml Approved signer endpoints, trusted public keys and the deployment default Workstation fallback ~/.config/heartwood/checkpoint-signers.toml Local development or offline signer profiles Signer credential Separate owner-only file Optional bearer token for signer requests Signing key Remote KMS, HSM or isolated local signer process Private key material, never project state

HEARTWOOD_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_REGISTRY names one absolute registry path where /etc is unavailable. Heartwood loads the explicit path first, then the system registry, then the user fallback, and never merges registries. The Carina launcher preserves an explicit registry path inside a Slurm allocation without exporting the signer token or provider credentials. A project cannot define an endpoint, key, credential or private-key path, so copying a project cannot redirect signing.

items.title: Configure a Production Signer
items.text:
Expose the signer contract through an authenticated HTTPS service backed by a key management service (KMS) or hardware security module (HSM). It accepts heartwood.audit-checkpoint-sign-request.v1 at /v1/checkpoints/sign and returns heartwood.audit-checkpoint-signature.v1, using Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 (DER-encoded). The service must authorize the deployment through a principal unavailable to agent tools, validate deployment and retention identifiers, restrict key use, rate-limit requests and keep provider audit records; it must not be an unrestricted signing oracle.

schema_version = "heartwood.checkpoint-signer-registry.v1"
default_profile = "research-records"

[profiles.research-records]
mode = "production"
endpoint = "https://checkpoint-signer.example.org/v1/checkpoints/sign"
signer_id = "research-records"
key_id = "heartwood-audit"
key_version = "2026-08"
algorithm = "ecdsa-p256-sha256"
public_key_sha256 = "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
trusted_public_key = "/etc/heartwood/keys/heartwood-audit-2026-08.pem"
authorization_token_file = "/run/secrets/heartwood-checkpoint-signer-token"
timeout_seconds = 15

authorization_token_file is optional when an authenticated proxy protects the route. An owner-only token file is readable by every process running as that owner, so use one only when agent tools cannot run as that identity; otherwise enforce authorization in a separate proxy and omit the token. All paths are absolute; the registry and public key must not be writable by others and the token must be an owner-only regular file. Heartwood rejects symbolic links, oversized files, changed key fingerprints, unapproved algorithms, insecure production endpoints and unknown fields. Signing uses the bundled public certificate authorities, ignores environment proxy and certificate settings and rejects redirects; trusted_ca_bundle adds a private CA file without replacing the pinned verification key.

List the profiles visible to a project, return to the default, or select another approved profile:

heartwood audit signer list
heartwood audit signer default
heartwood audit signer select research-records

Only the profile name is written to config.toml in the state directory. A deployment that permits no choice publishes one profile.

items.title: Use the Explicit Local Fallback
items.text:
Development and offline environments can run the bundled signer on a private Unix socket:

heartwood signer init-local
heartwood signer serve-local
heartwood audit signer select local-development

init-local creates a user registry, trusted public key, owner-only token and owner-only Ed25519 key under ~/.config/heartwood/, refuses to replace existing material and prints the next commands. Run serve-local in a separate terminal and select the profile in the project that creates checkpoints. The client validates the socket's owner, permissions and owner-only directory before sending the token, and there is no TCP fallback. After an abnormal shutdown, confirm the signer has stopped before removing its stale socket. These files are readable by unsandboxed processes running as the same user, so local verification is not independent of the account.

items.title: Verify and Checkpoint a Session
items.text:
Run these commands from the project that owns the session:

heartwood --session-id session-main audit verify

heartwood --session-id session-main audit checkpoint \
  --output /records/heartwood/session-main-2026-08-02 \
  --deployment-id research-environment \
  --retention-policy research-audit-7y \
  --retain-until 2033-08-02

Creation records an audit-export event, verifies the session and audit streams, canonicalizes the export, asks the active signer to sign, verifies the returned identity and signature, and publishes the directory atomically. The output must be outside the project and must not exist.

Verify a copied or restored checkpoint against the active profile, or against a separately retained public key:

heartwood audit verify-checkpoint /records/heartwood/session-main-2026-08-02
heartwood audit verify-checkpoint /records/heartwood/session-main-2026-08-02 \
  --public-key /records/trust/heartwood-audit-2026-08.pem

Verification rejects altered audit content, a broken chain, changed signed metadata, an invalid signature, an unexpected file, noncanonical encoding or a mismatched key.

items.title: Retain Experiment Records
items.text:
Add --include-experiments to retain the project's experiment records in the same checkpoint:

heartwood --session-id session-main audit checkpoint \
  --include-experiments \
  --output /records/heartwood/session-main-with-experiments \
  --deployment-id research-environment \
  --retention-policy research-audit-7y \
  --retain-until 2033-08-02

The gateway verifies and snapshots the records of every session in the project, records only the snapshot's digest, size, filename and binding format in the audit, and retains the export as experiments.jsonl. An empty project produces a bound empty export, not a claim that analyses completed. heartwood audit verify-checkpoint also rejects a missing or altered experiment export, an unbound file, or a binding that does not belong to the terminal audit-export event.

If signing fails, restore the signer and retry with a new output path; this adds another audit-export event but does not rerun an analysis. If a directory exists after an interrupted publication, verify it before choosing a new destination. Experiment metadata can include project-relative paths, declared actor references and environment fingerprints, so include it only where the destination's access rules permit. The signature does not establish scientific correctness or authenticate a declared researcher.

items.title: Rotate Keys and Enforce Retention
items.text: Publish a new profile or key version before directing checkpoints to a rotated key, and keep retired public keys mapped to their profile for as long as their checkpoints must verify. Never replace a public key in place under the same key version. The records system, not Heartwood, enforces access control, immutability, backup, replication, legal hold, expiration and deletion. Before production use, restore a retained checkpoint in a synthetic test, verify it, and confirm that the records system applies the declared policy.

items.title: Qualify Parallel Reviews
items.text: Parallel review runs independent advisory specialists on the same analysis concurrently. It does not authorize file changes, replace the parent agent, or relax action review. A deployment offers it only for a route whose retained trials show a speed improvement without lower review quality or excessive resource use; without that evidence, review stays sequential.

items.title: Establish Evidence
items.text:
Use the research evaluation harness in dedicated synthetic projects. Run matched sequential and parallel trials against the maintained planning-review suite, with the same model revision, runtime, Skills, fixtures, seed, and work budget. Retain complete EvaluationRun records, including failed and interrupted trials. The default gate requires three matching repetitions per case, evidence no older than 30 days, all required checks, known usage and cost, at least a 10% latency improvement, no more than 25% additional tokens or reported cost, and at most eight workers. Deterministic tests cannot qualify a real provider.

The typed ReviewQualification contract contains the suite, covered case, sequential and parallel configurations, policy, and retained records. ReviewQualifications groups approved route entries in one JSON document. Construct these models from the existing harness records; do not manufacture successful checks or set an eligibility flag. Two entries matching the same runtime and stage are ambiguous and rejected.

The gateway verifies the observed SDK version, model options, policy, context limits, scoped tool behavior, and specialist catalog against the retained runtime fingerprint. The operator verifies the remote model revision, hardware, precision, Skill tree and harness revision. Changing the deployed build or a remote service behind an unchanged model name requires reassessment; the fingerprint is not remote-server or binary attestation.

items.title: Configure the Gateway
items.text:
Install the JSON file outside every Heartwood project, in an operator-controlled location such as /etc/heartwood/review-qualifications.json. It must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, and must not be writable by group or other users. Mount it read-only in containers and deny the agent execution identity write access using platform controls. Supply its absolute path when starting Heartwood:

export HEARTWOOD_REVIEW_QUALIFICATIONS=/etc/heartwood/review-qualifications.json
heartwood

Use the same environment setting for the browser server or notebook kernel. Do not store this configuration in .heartwood/ or expose a browser upload for it. Embedding applications may instead inject the existing trusted parallel_review_preparer; configuring both sources is rejected.

Evidence is an operator trust decision

The file contains retained measurements, not a cryptographically authenticated qualification certificate. A schema-valid file is not proof that a trial occurred. Review the originating run and preserve its provenance before installing it. An external path and file permissions do not isolate an agent running as the same operating-system user; use a separate identity or read-only mount for maintained deployments.

items.title: Review and Revoke
items.text:
The researcher selects Preview Parallel Review and reviews the exact workers and work limits before consenting. Normal grouped tool approval is still required. The gateway re-reads evidence and checks runtime ownership during preparation and native dispatch; it does not use a cached success flag. Offered limits cannot exceed the maintained stage or the retained case budgets.

Remove the file to prevent new parallel admissions, or replace it atomically with reviewed evidence. Stale, missing, malformed, ambiguous, or changed evidence cannot authorize new work. After an update, refresh the preview and obtain new consent when its identity changes. Removing evidence does not undo completed actions or forcibly stop already admitted work; use the normal pause or cancellation controls for active work. Sequential review remains available through Review Analysis.

items.title: Platform Contract
items.text:
A research platform can embed Heartwood as its research interaction layer while keeping authority over identity, compute, storage, inference and spending. This contract states what each side provides, how the contract is versioned, and how to check an integration against it. Platform API and Access Requirements turns it into an access request for a specific platform.

Each part is marked with one status:

  • Current: implemented, tested, and exported as a current artifact.
  • Draft: an exported schema with offline checks; Heartwood does not send or consume the message at runtime.
  • Unavailable: neither implemented nor exported.

A schema describes a message; it does not enable a service, authorize a request, or establish that a deployment is qualified.

items.title: Scope and Status
items.text: Part Status Hosting the published artifact with persistent project storage Current Access and identity through an authenticated proxy and the launch capability Current for one launching principal per gateway; per-user identity verification unavailable Deployment policy bound by the operator deployment manifest Current Inference through built-in and operator-configured routes Current; connection-manifest startup unavailable; model metadata draft Agent isolation of the complete worker Current for the OpenShell Docker reference adapter; qualified only against the qualification-only sandbox gateway build Controlled data controls Selected read-only inputs current; quarantine and steward-approved release unavailable Audit and records Signed checkpoints and deployment-bound evidence current; signer and records-service qualification is the platform's Platform services over MCP, outside operations, launch context and budgets Draft; the content-bound outside operation authorization is current, but no outside-service adapter ships and built-in launchers install none Hosted per-project gateways with verified OpenID Connect identity Unavailable Realtime voice Unavailable

items.title: Responsibilities
items.text:
Area Heartwood Platform Researcher identity Records the launching principal as the actor of every accepted command and ignores actors claimed in requests Authenticates the person, authorizes project access, ends the session Gateway access Requires the launch capability on every request and validates the declared ingress route Routes only authenticated users to the gateway, strips client-supplied forwarding and identity headers, terminates TLS, delivers the capability Research session Owns canonical session records, action review, outside authorization and interface projections Keeps the gateway, research files, protected state and network route available Policy Evaluates model routes, review modes and credential references against the deployment ceiling Defines the ceiling and enforces filesystem, process and network restrictions Inference Selects an authorized route; keeps credentials out of model context, tool inputs, events and exports Operates endpoints, enforces account, model and tenant authorization, data-use agreements and spend limits Agent isolation Admits, fences and revokes worker attempts; admits worker responses against what it sent Provides the sandbox, its control plane, and credential substitution outside the worker Platform services Defines draft messages and offline checks; binds outside operations to researcher decisions Authorizes every call; owns scheduling, quotas, cost, entitlements and infrastructure policy Project and billing context Binds the research directory and state through the deployment manifest Selects the platform project and billing or grant attribution Audit and provenance Writes content-minimized audit and experiment records and requests signed checkpoints Authorizes the signer, retains records immutably, keeps its own operation audit Controlled data Makes no compliance claim Decides data eligibility, agreements, egress, monitoring and incident response

Platform authentication does not replace gateway controls, and a Heartwood approval never grants platform authority.

items.title: Interfaces
items.text:
Direction Interface Authority Researcher interface → gateway Generated gateway OpenAPI, server-sent events and WebSocket Gateway validates ingress, capability, commands and approvals Worker → inference transport → provider Existing provider API and model identifiers Transport holds the credential and routes; provider authorizes account, model and tenant Trusted adapter → platform service Existing platform APIs; optionally MCP under the draft profile Platform authenticates each call and enforces project, dataset, compute and billing permissions Launcher → sandbox infrastructure Existing infrastructure control API Operator owns admission, policy, runtime identity and revocation Gateway → signer and records service Checkpoint-signing HTTPS interface and S3-compatible object storage Signer authorizes publication; records service enforces scoped access and retention

The contract reuses existing standards and adds only what Heartwood needs:

Area Upstream definition Heartwood addition Inference Provider APIs supported by the SDK, including Chat Completions and Responses Route eligibility, model metadata declarations Platform tools MCP discovery, calls, results, errors and capabilities Required annotations, policy checks, review of side effects Jobs, workflows and data Native scheduler and storage APIs; GA4GH TES, WES and DRS where supported References linking native resources to proposals, estimates and audit records Cost FOCUS definitions Workload assumptions, estimate coverage and validity, budget observations Asynchronous results MCP Tasks extension, revision 2026-07-28 Estimate payload carried in task results

Upstream definitions stay authoritative for their own messages, streaming, errors and lifecycle; the bundle pins their revisions instead of copying them.

items.title: Hosting
items.text:
Required:

  • Run the published image or native release without replacing its entrypoint, user or bundled browser assets.
  • Provide persistent research storage and separate state storage with native advisory locks; object-store and file-transfer mounts are not session stores unless qualified.
  • Keep model weights, credentials and deployment secrets out of image layers and the project directory.
  • Keep the owner-only Unix sockets and directories of a Heartwood-managed model server and of a local checkpoint signer outside worker access.

Recommended:

  • Verify the release's build attestations before admitting an artifact, and back up project storage across compute replacement.

Optional:

  • Provide Jupyter where the platform offers the notebook bridge.

Releases carry build attestations; separate artifact signatures, software bills of materials and third-party notice bundles are unavailable for release images and native assets.

Topology Runs the gateway Authenticates the person Status Workstation or container The researcher The operating system and the launch link Current Platform workspace The platform, in the researcher's workspace The platform proxy Current for the Terra terminal and notebook and the Stanford Carina terminal, CI validated Hosted per-project service The platform, one gateway per researcher and project The institution's identity provider, verified by Heartwood Unavailable

Gateway shutdown does not stop external jobs or storage charges.

items.title: Access and Identity
items.text:
Required:

  • Authenticate every user before traffic reaches the gateway, and restrict the gateway's network route to the platform proxy.
  • Remove client-supplied forwarding and identity headers before setting the proxy's own values.
  • Deliver the launch capability, either by letting the researcher open the one-time launch link, or by injecting X-Heartwood-Capability for requests the platform has already authenticated.
  • Keep the capability away from the agent workspace, the worker, other users and logs.

Recommended:

  • Run one gateway per researcher and project; Heartwood records one launching principal per gateway and does not distinguish people who share it.
  • Serve mutually untrusted projects on separate origins; base paths on one origin do not isolate browser storage.

A proxy that injects the capability authenticates on the researcher's behalf and must do so only for the user who owns that gateway. For example, a proxy at https://research.example.org that strips the prefix /heartwood/project-a and connects from 10.0.0.2 starts the gateway with a secret from its secret manager:

heartwood gateway serve --capability-fd 3 3</run/secrets/heartwood-capability \
  --ingress-mode trusted-proxy \
  --host 10.0.0.5 \
  --port 8767 \
  --public-origin https://research.example.org \
  --base-path /heartwood/project-a \
  --trusted-proxy-source 10.0.0.2/32 \
  --proxy-strips-prefix

The proxy then adds X-Heartwood-Capability with the same secret to each authenticated request. Gateway Ingress and Launch Capability state the exact validation rules, and the command reference lists every serve option.

items.title: Deployment Policy
items.text:
Required:

  • Bind each managed project through an operator-owned deployment manifest outside research files and state.
  • List exact model and catalog endpoints, credential references and permitted review modes, with egress denied by default.
  • Enforce filesystem, process and network restrictions outside Heartwood; policy validation cannot constrain a compromised process.

Recommended:

  • List only review-all in allowed_action_review_modes until each further mode has been evaluated for the platform; the default when the key is omitted permits all three.

Optional:

  • Publish approved Skill sources through the deployment-owned registry at /etc/heartwood/skill-sources.toml; only that registry can approve a Skill for controlled data.

Project settings can narrow the ceiling but cannot widen endpoints, credentials, capability tiers or review modes, lower the aggregate-count floor, disable default-deny egress or change the platform identifier. Without a manifest, the platform adapter's built-in policy applies and state stays in the research directory.

items.title: Inference
items.text:
Required:

  • An OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint with streaming and native tool calls for compatible services; provider-specific routes keep their SDK-supported protocols.
  • A model list endpoint that returns only the models the authenticated identity may use.
  • Platform-held credentials, through a managed identity, a process-only variable or a mounted file outside the project.
  • A statement of which data classes each route may receive; compatibility does not establish eligibility.
  • Distinguishable failures for rejected credentials, exhausted quota, rate limits, invalid model configuration and temporary unavailability.

Required for isolated workers:

  • An outside inference transport that substitutes the credential, provider-side enforcement of the approved account, model set and tenant even when several models share one hostname, and an operator-configured credential lifetime and rotation; Heartwood sets no expiry on it.

Recommended:

  • The Responses API where the model supports it; Heartwood selects the protocol per model from the OpenHands model capabilities.

Optional:

  • Compute on which Heartwood runs a managed model, and an approved process to import verified model bundles.

Heartwood discovers models through a policy-checked catalog endpoint and never implements a second provider proxy. The heartwood.model-connections.v1 schema describes deployment-owned connections, but startup does not load a connection manifest, and the OpenHands model table does not recognize platform model aliases. The draft model-metadata supplement declares, per model identity:

Field Meaning Level Model identifier The exact value sent in each request Required Protocols Chat Completions, Responses or both Required Context and token limits Context window and input and output limits; missing values stay unknown Recommended Tool calling Whether native tool calls are supported Required Data classes Classes the route may receive under the platform's agreements Required Deprecation Whether the model is being withdrawn, so no model is silently substituted Recommended

items.title: Agent Isolation
items.text:
For an isolated worker, the platform provides:

Required:

  • A sandbox with mandatory filesystem and process restrictions, resource limits, deny-by-default network enforcement, and a control plane the worker cannot reach.
  • Read-only projections of selected inputs and verified Skills, a private writable workspace, and no research-directory, protected-state or Docker-socket mount.
  • Provider credentials, signing authority, launch capabilities, management sockets and peer-worker state outside worker access.
  • Authenticated admission bound to project, session, attempt and runtime identity, with a changed generation or configuration fencing the old attempt.
  • Revocation observed outside the worker before replacement or writer release, with reconciliation instead of duplicate execution when creation or deletion is uncertain.
  • A sandbox gateway that provides the deletion behavior native qualification depends on, with its version declared in gateway_versions.

The reference adapter uses OpenShell on a local Docker engine with the native OpenHands remote conversation, workspace and event contracts. OpenShell names, policy objects and control credentials belong to that adapter, not to portable platform messages; another adapter must keep the same authority, lifecycle and evidence properties on its own infrastructure. Worker-reported events and output are untrusted: they cannot create approvals, authorize platform operations or prove that the worker has stopped. Sandbox Enforcement and Gateway Enforcement divide these controls between the two sides.

items.title: Controlled Data
items.text:
Required:

  • Decide data eligibility for every model route, dataset and interface.
  • Provide read-only input snapshots, enforced egress denial and ephemeral, encrypted execution storage for controlled work.
  • Keep outputs in quarantine until an authorized data steward approves an exact release manifest.

Heartwood provides the selected-input transfer: the manifest's [worker.inputs] binds each file's path, size and SHA-256, at most 128 files, 16 MiB per file and 64 MiB in total. Staging rereads and verifies the bytes, rejects symbolic links, multiply linked and nonregular files, excludes .git and .heartwood, and uses a private directory outside the project that is removed when staging ends. File digests establish content identity, not authorization to disclose the content. Heartwood provides no quarantine, encrypted storage or steward-approved release, and is not a controlled-data boundary on its own; see Security and Controlled Data.

items.title: Audit and Records
items.text:
Recommended:

  • A deployment-owned checkpoint signer, installed through /etc/heartwood/checkpoint-signers.toml or HEARTWOOD_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_REGISTRY, with keys no agent can use.
  • Retention, immutability and deletion enforcement for exported audit and experiment records.

Required for managed evidence:

  • An independently authorized signer that retains each checkpoint before returning it, and a versioned, retention-locked records service with separate identities for the gateway and the signer.

Required for platform services:

  • An operation audit log joinable to Heartwood's audit by operation reference.

The signer interface is POST /v1/checkpoints/sign, accepting heartwood.audit-checkpoint-sign-request.v1 and returning heartwood.audit-checkpoint-signature.v1 over HTTPS. Audit Checkpoints and Retention defines the registry, the evidence table and the storage permissions.

items.title: Platform Services
items.text: The service, operation, task and budget messages are draft. Heartwood disables MCP servers in its OpenHands configuration and advertises no platform service.

items.title: Service Discovery
items.text:
Required:

  • Expose services over MCP Streamable HTTP with a stable server identity.
  • Describe each tool's purpose, input and output schemas, and required permission; read access never implies permission to allocate resources or attach data.
  • Annotate each tool with explicit boolean readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint values.
  • Enforce identity, quotas and dataset entitlements on every call, independently of Heartwood's approval.
  • Accept delegated or platform-held credentials that never reach model context, tool environments or exports.

Annotations are hints from the server, not authorization, and a changed tool set requires a new review.

items.title: Operations That Change Platform State
items.text:
A tool that allocates compute, submits work, attaches data or starts an application is an operation.

Required:

  • Before approval, return a proposal with resource limits, expected duration, estimated cost when available, data scope and destination.
  • Accept a caller-supplied operation identifier, scoped to the authorized project and service and bound to the exact proposal; a repeat with the same contents is the same operation, and different contents under the same identifier are a conflict.
  • An estimate or preparation call that persists data, incurs charges or reserves resources follows the normal review and authorization path.
  • Report status by operation identifier, so an uncertain outcome is reconciled rather than resubmitted.
  • Report cancellation as the observed result, without promising rollback.
  • Return a reference that joins the platform's audit record to Heartwood's session audit without copying payloads.
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Submitted
    Submitted --> Denied: platform refuses
    Submitted --> Queued: platform accepts
    Submitted --> Running
    Submitted --> Completed: immediate result
    Submitted --> Failed
    Submitted --> Unknown: response lost
    Queued --> Running
    Queued --> Cancelled
    Queued --> Failed
    Unknown --> Denied: status reconciled
    Unknown --> Queued: status reconciled
    Unknown --> Running: status reconciled
    Unknown --> Completed: status reconciled
    Unknown --> Failed: status reconciled
    Unknown --> Cancelled: status reconciled
    Running --> Completed
    Running --> Failed
    Running --> Cancelled: cancellation observed
    Denied --> [*]
    Completed --> [*]
    Failed --> [*]
    Cancelled --> [*]

These states are what Heartwood shows; keep native backend states and references alongside them. Unknown means Heartwood has no authoritative observation, not that nothing happened, and a cancelled operation can leave completed work and incurred charges.

items.title: Asynchronous Results
items.text:
Pending results use the MCP Tasks extension, revision 2026-07-28, exported unchanged with its pinned commit, checksum and license.

  • The server advertises io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks under capabilities.extensions, and each task-enabled tools/call opts in through params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions.
  • A call returns either the immediate tool result or a flat resultType: "task" handle.
  • tasks/get returns status and, when completed, the original tool result, whose structuredContent uses the same estimate schema as the immediate path.
  • tasks/update supplies requested input and does not bypass review or authorization.
  • tasks/cancel acknowledges a request; observe the task, backend operation and spending separately afterward.

A completed task can carry a tool result with isError: true. Expired or missing task state requires reconciliation by operation identifier before resubmission. mcp-tasks.SOURCE.txt records where the profile interprets differences between upstream prose and examples.

items.title: Launch Context, Budgets and Estimates
items.text:
The platform owns project selection, billing attribution, spending thresholds, reservations, accounting and enforcement. Heartwood compares estimates the platform produces; it does not price work, monitor spending or cap bills. A draft heartwood.platform-launch-context.v1 document carries the platform-owned binding:

{
  "schema_version": "heartwood.platform-launch-context.v1",
  "project_context_id": "launch-synthetic-1",
  "platform_id": "synthetic-platform",
  "project_id": "research-project-a",
  "billing_attribution_ref": "binding-a",
  "authority_ref": "platform-authority",
  "policy_ref": "policy-v1",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-17T10:00:00Z"
}

Keep it outside agent-writable state; possession of a copy does not authenticate its issuer. It is separate from the deployment manifest, which binds only the research directory, state and policy.

fixtures/synthetic/platform-contract/ contains a complete exchange for an exploration, a batch and an inference workload, plus mcp-tasks.json with immediate and deferred estimates and a cancellation followed by continued backend work. Read each exchange in this order:

  1. prediction: quantities, units, assumptions and project-local evidence for one plan revision.
  2. estimates: platform prices for that prediction; scope distinguishes a plan from an element quote, and coverage states how complete the cost information is.
  3. operation_sets: exact native-request references, hard limits and embedded estimate snapshots for review.
  4. researcher_decisions: the decision bound to the proposal revision and document hash; the platform's own decision is in authorizations.
  5. operations and budgets: separately observed execution and accounting state, including unknown or stale values.

Rules for these messages:

  • An estimate total already includes components marked included_in_total; separate estimates for the same work are alternatives, not additive charges.
  • Amounts are decimal strings; null is unknown and "0" is an explicit zero; denominations must match before comparison, and Heartwood performs no conversion.
  • The proposal digest is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 document bytes, not a canonical JSON form; reserializing requires a new binding and decision.
  • reviewed_operation_set() rejects duplicate JSON keys, and verify_reviewed_operation_set() checks a stored envelope against the original bytes.
  • An estimate, a researcher approval, a platform authorization and a spending reservation are distinct states, and approving a plan does not authorize each operation in it.

Price and cost fields reuse FOCUS definitions from the SKU Price proposal at revision 005a30566a754db4e0f346d20c7063daba579080 and the estimation-features proposal at revision a2f9f93cb618ab490b90098d0456dfcdb813c5e7; these are draft references, not a claim of FOCUS 1.5 conformance.

Requirement FOCUS definition or boundary Rate amount and basis UnitPrice and UnitPriceType, preserving decimal precision and distinguishing list, base and contracted rates Measurement scale PricingUnit; a token count is not a million-token pricing quantity Denomination PricingCurrency, distinguishing currency or credits from resource quantities Price identity and period The SKU Price dataset's provider, SKU, contract and price-period context Price eligibility SkuPriceEligibility, which describes pricing, not authority to use a resource Workload, coverage and decisions Heartwood interaction records, not FOCUS columns Observation time and estimate expiry Platform interaction records, not the price's effective period

items.title: Gateway API
items.text:
gateway.openapi.json defines every REST operation, the launch-token exchange, server-sent events and, under x-websocket, the WebSocket transport, generated from the typed contracts. The Gateway API reference explains command envelopes, approval targets, retries and recovery.

  • HTTP requests carry X-Heartwood-Capability; capability cookies are not accepted.
  • A browser WebSocket sends {"type": "authenticate", "capability": "…"} as its first frame within five seconds; a trusted proxy may inject the header instead.
  • Clients resume streams with the after query cursor; Last-Event-ID replay is not implemented.
  • During shutdown, new REST and event-stream requests receive 503, WebSockets close with code 1012, and the terminal exits with code 75; reconnect to the next gateway with the last cursor.
  • Project maintenance or a conflicting owner returns 409 or closes WebSockets with 1012; it is not permission to start a second writer.
  • Session command payloads are JSON objects validated by their command handlers.

Proxies must support unbuffered streaming and WebSocket upgrades. A successful HTTP exchange does not establish that an asynchronous research action completed.

items.title: Outside Operation Admission
items.text:
A trusted Python embedding can connect platform services to the research session. It supplies a session-scoped ExternalActionAdapter through SessionGateway(external_actions_factory=...) and the SDK ClientToolSpec definitions through native_worker_plan_factory(client_tools=...). The worker registers those tools; their acknowledgement proposes an operation and does not execute it. No production outside-service adapter ships with Heartwood: heartwood gateway serve and the other built-in launchers install none, and the gateway has no HTTP route for registering adapters or creating proposals. The interface is exercised only by embedding launchers such as the native qualification fixture.

To offer outside operations, a platform or embedding launcher must provide:

  • a launcher that constructs SessionGateway with protected state from a deployment manifest and an owned native worker;
  • an ExternalActionAdapter implementation for its services, holding the service credentials outside the worker;
  • the exact ClientToolSpec definitions for the proposal tools, whose canonical schemas are bound into the worker input identity;
  • trusted input storage for read_input that does not follow worker-selected paths; and
  • a destination service that authenticates the adapter and enforces entitlement, project scope, expiry and idempotency itself.

The adapter's contract:

  • prepare resolves the native request and immutable input references with no external effect;
  • check_policy and check_result_policy raise when current policy or the actor's entitlement forbids dispatch or disclosure;
  • read_input returns bounded bytes from trusted storage, which the gateway verifies before use;
  • submit sends once and independently enforces actor, project, live attempt, policy, expiry and content binding, so a repeated operation identifier never creates a second effect;
  • observe queries an existing operation without submitting; and
  • prepare_result returns sanitized JSON through the service's own authorization, without credentials.

SessionService.propose_external_action turns a retained worker proposal into a review with a gateway-issued operation identifier, the complete request, input digests, destination, worker identity, policy revision and a five-minute validity interval. The approve and deny commands bind the full proposal digest. Immediately before submission the gateway rechecks the live worker attempt, project, policy, actor entitlement, validity and input contents, and submits the verified bytes without reopening worker paths.

The decision and submission intent are journaled before the service is contacted; with managed evidence, the authorization is retained outside first, even in buffered mode. An approved operation that could not be sent is sent only by an exact retry of its own approval command; status reads, reconciliation and automatic decisions never send it. Denial withdraws an authorization that has not been submitted; an undispatched authorization that reaches the end of its validity interval is recorded as expired and never sent. After a review expires, propose_external_action for the same worker proposal records the expiry and issues a new identifier and review. reconcile_external_actions queries the existing operation after an interruption and never resubmits; an observation must match project, service, operation and proposal digest. Denying an already submitted operation does not cancel it.

The audit records operation identifiers, digests, decisions and status without request or input payloads. The service must independently authenticate the caller and enforce entitlement, project scope, attempt revocation, policy, expiry and idempotency, and the worker must have no other route to it.

items.title: Result Release to the Worker
items.text:
Approving an outside operation does not authorize disclosing its result. SessionService.propose_external_result reads the result of a terminal, observed operation from the current worker attempt and opens a separate review that binds the exact result, the observation, worker identity, policy revision, declared model identifier and route, and a fresh five-minute validity interval. Results are limited to 64 KiB including the provenance envelope, and ambiguous JSON is rejected. Approval requires current disclosure policy, the live worker lease and an idle conversation.

The release reaches the model as a user-role message whose JSON envelope labels it as an outside result; that label is not an instruction boundary. There is one open release review per operation, denial is final for it, and an interrupted delivery is never retried automatically.

items.title: Failure States
items.text:
Condition The platform returns Heartwood shows Capability not offered No advertised support The choice is hidden in every interface Missing or invalid launch capability Not applicable HW-INGRESS-003 Request does not match the declared route Not applicable HW-INGRESS-002 Sandbox gateway version not declared Its Health version HW-WORKER-001 Expired or rejected model credential An authentication error HW-AGENT-008 Exhausted quota or budget A quota error HW-AGENT-009 Rate limit A rate-limit error with a retry interval when known HW-AGENT-010 Denied or misconfigured model A model or authorization error HW-AGENT-011 Service temporarily unavailable An unavailability error HW-AGENT-012

Diagnostics and Troubleshooting gives each code's recovery steps. Platform-operation failures have no runtime presentation because the operation profile is draft.

items.title: Security Properties
items.text:
Both sides must preserve these properties:

  1. Model output, tool output, service responses and dataset content cannot approve an action, widen policy or grant platform permissions.
  2. A Heartwood approval is necessary, never sufficient; the platform authorizes every call.
  3. Credentials never appear in project configuration, model context, tool environments, events, logs or exports.
  4. Service results, tool descriptions, annotations and platform responses are untrusted, bounded input.
  5. A timeout or lost response is resolved by status, never by resubmission.
  6. Egress is denied by default, and the platform network is the authoritative egress control.

items.title: Versioning
items.text:
The contract bundle follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 independently of the application; this release's bundle is 0.1.0, recorded as contract_version in contract.json.

  • Compatibility covers message structure, validation rules and documented behavior.
  • Before 1.0.0, a minor version may break compatibility and a patch preserves it; from 1.0.0, incompatible changes increment the major version.
