Source Meaning bundled Included and reviewed with this Heartwood release catalog source ID Offered as a signed, immutable package by a source the deployment configured installed Installed in this project from a catalog or a local directory Status Meaning active Given to the agent available Offered by a catalog and not installed revoked Withdrawn by its signed source and no longer given to the agent unsupported Not compatible with this platform; the reason is shown

The browser also labels each Skill as Repository reviewed or Local and unreviewed, and says whether the deployment approved it for controlled data.

items.title: Add a Reviewed Skill
items.text:
Refresh the configured sources, inspect the Skill, and install it:

heartwood skills refresh
heartwood skills inspect SKILL_NAME
heartwood skills install SKILL_NAME

Inspection shows the description, declared tools, network and data-access requirements, dataset types, download size, source, and exact content digest. The install command shows the current revision again and asks before continuing; it refreshes the signed source once more and stops if the content changed after your review. In the browser, select the review button next to an available Skill.

Non-interactive automation must supply the digest from inspection instead of approving whichever revision is current:

heartwood skills install SKILL_NAME \
  --approve \
  --expected-tree-sha256 sha256:DIGEST_FROM_INSPECTION

With more than one configured source, add --source SOURCE_ID to refresh, inspect, or install.

items.title: Add a Skill From This Project
items.text:
A maintainer can install a complete Agent Skill directory from inside the project. Its content has not passed repository review:

heartwood skills inspect-local ./skills/my-skill
heartwood skills install-local ./skills/my-skill

Heartwood rejects paths outside the project or inside .heartwood/, copies the complete directory without following links, binds the approval to its exact digest, and labels it Local and unreviewed in every interface. The same interactive confirmation and digest options apply.

items.title: Remove a Skill
items.text:
heartwood skills remove SKILL_NAME

Removal deactivates the Skill, records the change, and resets open sessions so they no longer use it. If unexpected files sit beside an installed Skill, Heartwood stops listing Skills and starting sessions until they are removed, and the error names the directory to clean up.

items.title: Scope of Skill Approval
items.text:
Installing a Skill grants no file, network, credential, model, or platform permission. Action review, the project boundary, process permissions, and deployment policy still apply to everything the agent does with it.

Repository review is not controlled-data approval. Only a deployment can approve an exact Skill digest for controlled data, and the interfaces report that decision separately.

See Skill Trust and Distribution for the verification model and Configuration and State for configuring sources.

items.title: Use Research Specialists
items.text: A research specialist gives the agent a focused second pass on one part of a research task and returns its result to the conversation.

items.title: Ask for a Specialist Review
items.text:
Name the review you want in your request:

Before changing files, ask the Research Planner to identify the inputs, assumptions, and verification steps. Then implement only the approved plan and ask the Reproducibility Reviewer to assess the final evidence.

When the agent delegates, the delegation appears as a Specialist Review action in the pending action set. Check the specialist name and the delegated objective before allowing the set; no review mode allows a specialist task without you. When the specialist finishes, its result returns to the agent, which decides how to continue.

Heartwood runs one specialist at a time by default and records its lifecycle, lineage, usage, and result in the session that every interface shows. Each delegation is a fresh review of the evidence the agent supplies; ask for another review when the evidence changes.

Use Pause in the browser, /pause in the terminal, or session.pause() in a notebook to request cancellation of active specialist work. Cancellation does not undo completed actions, and the model provider may still process and bill a request it already accepted.

items.title: Available Reviews
items.text:
Specialist Focus Verified Skills Research Planner A sequential plan, assumptions, inputs, checks, and required evidence None Data Quality Reviewer Completeness, validity, temporal consistency, duplicates, and denominators omop-cohort-summary Cohort and Feature Reviewer Eligibility, timing, censoring, feature construction, and leakage omop-cohort-summary Statistical Reviewer Estimands, splits, specification, uncertainty, validation, and interpretation baseline-model Reproducibility Reviewer Revisions, environments, parameters, execution, artifacts, and verification omop-cohort-summary, baseline-model, aggregate-export

Specialists are advisory. They see only the evidence the agent passes to them and cannot read files, run commands, use the network, or change the project. Each has a model-step limit and usage budget, uses the active model route, and can use only the verified Skills listed for it.

The catalog also lists Analysis Implementer as not available. A specialist with project tools would need its own actions to appear in your review and to recover safely after a restart, which the OpenHands task interface does not provide.

items.title: See the Catalog
items.text:
• Terminal: heartwood specialists outside a session, or /specialists inside one.
  • Browser: Specialists in the session navigation.
  • Notebook: session.specialist_settings().

items.title: Read Specialist Results
items.text:
Specialist output is model-generated review, not independent scientific validation. Inspect the evidence and apply the same domain, statistical, and reproducibility review as for work you produced yourself.

In a research workflow, specialists also return structured findings, shown as Unverified review proposals in every interface. A proposal names something to check; it does not establish a defect or authorize a correction, and no proposals is not proof that the analysis is correct. If a specialist cannot supply its required structured result, Heartwood reports the task as failed instead of accepting the summary. A deployment can also offer a qualified parallel review for workflow stages with several reviewers; it gives specialists no additional tools.

The audit export records specialist lifecycle and usage, not the delegated instructions or returned text.

items.title: Use the Terminal
items.text: The terminal works on every supported platform and is the only interface on Stanford Carina.

items.title: Start a Session
items.text:
cd /path/to/project
heartwood

Type a request at the prompt and press Enter. While the model works, Heartwood shows an animated status and the elapsed time; it does not invent progress the model service does not report. Task Tracker progress, model activity, and specialist status appear when OpenHands supplies them.

When the agent proposes an action set, the interface lists every member and waits for your decision. Use the arrow keys and Enter to allow or reject the complete set; see Review an Action Set. After the work settles, Heartwood may offer up to two suggested next requests.

Heartwood falls back to the plain interface when the terminal cannot run the full-screen application.

items.title: Launch Options
items.text:
Command Result heartwood --session-id cohort-review Open or resume a named session instead of the main session heartwood --plain Use the line-oriented interface, for logs, basic terminals, and accessibility tools heartwood --review-mode review-changes Start with a review mode selected heartwood --prompt "..." Submit one request, wait for it, print the result, and exit

For example:

heartwood --prompt "Inspect this project and summarize its test failures. Do not modify files."

items.title: Steer Active Work
items.text:
While OpenHands runs, you can type further guidance for the active task or pause it. /pause pauses the run and /resume continues it. Pausing also stops automatic review decisions until you continue.

Enter /permissions to see which actions Heartwood allows without asking, or /permissions MODE to change it. Actions allowed under a review rule are shown as allowed automatically, with the rule.

items.title: Inspect Files and Changes
items.text:
The full-screen interface has three views:

Shortcut View Ctrl-1 Conversation and action review Ctrl-2 Project tree and read-only text files Ctrl-3 Changed files and read-only per-file diffs

Ctrl-P opens the command palette for these views, action review settings, status, replay, and audit export.

The Files view excludes .heartwood/ and .git/, does not follow symbolic links, and labels binary, unsupported, or truncated files. In a Git repository, the Changes view shows the Git changes. In a project without Git, it shows only successful file changes from typed file-editor actions in the selected session; it does not infer changes from terminal commands.

items.title: Conversation Commands
items.text:
Command Result /help Show the available commands /status Show model, credential, policy, and action-review status /permissions [MODE] Show or select the review mode: review-all, review-changes, or review-outside-effects /allow Allow the complete pending action set once /reject Reject the complete pending action set /pause Pause active work /resume Resume a paused session /specialists Show the research specialists available to the agent /workflows List the research workflows /workflow Set up a research workflow or show its current stage and next commands /experiments Show the experiment records of this session /files [DIRECTORY] List the project tree /show FILE Show one UTF-8 project file /changes [FILE] List changed paths or show one read-only diff /replay Show the persisted session history /audit-export Write a scrubbed JSON Lines audit export /exit Close the interface without deleting the session

In the plain interface, use these commands in place of keyboard selection; /allow and /reject apply to the set shown, without a tool-call identifier.

items.title: Stop and Return
items.text:
Use /exit to close the interface, or Ctrl-Q in the full-screen interface and Ctrl-C in the plain one. Run the same command in the same project to resume, with the same --session-id if you used one. A review mode selected during the session is not kept; the next launch starts at the default.

Only one process writes a session at a time. Close the terminal before continuing the same session in the browser or a notebook, or use a different session identifier there.
